input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility fixes for core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion, all four flows are fully operable with keyboard alone — no focus traps, no unreachable controls — and visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. This is the code deliverable that the updated conformance documentation will describe.

## Scope

- Fix each keyboard accessibility defect enumerated in the audit report for the four audited core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission):
  - Restore and manage focus correctly in modals (focus moved into the modal on open, trapped while open, returned to the invoking control on close).
  - Make every control in the audited flows reachable and operable via keyboard (tab order, arrow-key navigation where the pattern requires it, keyboard-activatable actions).
  - Apply the consistent visible focus indicator treatment across the audited flows so the indicator is uniform rather than varying per control or per page.
- Cover both keyboard operability (no focus traps, no unreachable controls) and focus-indicator consistency in the same pass over the same UI surfaces.
- Verify no regression to pointer-based interaction in the audited flows.
- Out of scope (per strategy): screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones. Incidental reference updates that fall out of these fixes (e.g. a changed control label referenced in nearby docs) are folded in here rather than split out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed start-to-finish using the keyboard alone.
- No focus traps exist in the audited flows: focus is managed into, within, and out of modals without keyboard users becoming stuck.
- No control in the audited flows is unreachable or inoperable via keyboard; every defect enumerated in the audit report for these flows is resolved or explicitly dispositioned with rationale.
- Visible focus indicators are consistent (uniform style and visibility) across all controls in the audited flows.
- Pointer-based interaction in the audited flows continues to work as before (no regressions).
- The Dashboard build pipeline (CI) is green with the changes included.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. Core scope of this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. Consolidated with HLR-1 in this epic: both requirements edit the same UI surfaces in the same four flows, so a split would double-touch the same components.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation — the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product documentation's accessibility statement — to reflect the fixed keyboard-accessibility state of the four core Dashboard flows. Two public-sector customers require the updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the published documentation is a first-class deliverable of the strategy, not an incidental follow-up.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT conformance entries for the four audited core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) to reflect the remediated keyboard operability and focus-indicator state, based on the shipped implementation.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the current accessibility posture of the audited flows.
- Republish both artifacts through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Technical review of the updated content against the implemented behavior before publication.
- Content topics:
  - VPAT: keyboard operability and focus visibility entries for the four flows.
  - Accessibility statement: current statement of conformance for the audited flows and any remaining known limitations that are in scope to disclose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the fixed keyboard-accessibility state of the four audited core flows and republished.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished to reflect the same fixed state.
- The updated content has been technically reviewed against the implemented behavior (reviewed by the implementing team or equivalent technical reviewer) before publication, per the strategy's "with technical review" requirement.
- The published statement is consistent with what was actually implemented — no conformance claims beyond the shipped fixes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. Entire scope of this epic.

- **Below-threshold (Check 1)** does not apply: the scope spans two components (Dashboard, Documentation) and two architecturally distinct work streams — code implementation in the Dashboard UI and substantive documentation content authoring (VPAT update + accessibility statement republish, HLR-3). ## Decomposition Analysis

- **Step 1 (parse)**: The strategy uses a simplified format — Affected Components is a bare list (no change descriptions or owner teams), and there is no Impacted Teams table, Dependencies table, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, or Non-Functional Requirements section. Recorded as health warnings; decomposition proceeds on available information. The Dashboard owner team (RHOAI Dashboard) is taken from the architecture context file; the Documentation owner team is inferred as RHOAI Documentation (no owner stated in the strategy).

Dashboard exists in architecture context (`architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`, GA, Konflux onboarded), so no onboarding chain is needed. Documentation has no architecture-context file; this does not trigger a provisioning chain because it is an existing Red Hat docs content process (routed via `docs-authoring`), not a new platform component being onboarded.
- **Step 3 (investigations)**: The strategy states "None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow." No open questions, risks, pending reviews, or conditional ADRs appear elsewhere in the strategy. No Investigation epics.
- **Step 4 (HLR mapping)**: HLR-1 (keyboard operability) and HLR-2 (consistent focus indicators) both target the same four audited flows in the same component and team — they edit the same UI surfaces and are consolidated into E001 (both P1, no priority split needed). - **Tiered delivery**: Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing.
- **Rules 23–25**: Rule 23 (rollback/feature-flag) not applicable — the strategy fixes accessibility defects in existing flows, it does not replace an existing capability. Rule 24 (technical review AC) applied to E002, matching HLR-3's "with technical review" requirement. Rule 25: no `konflux-onboarding` epic exists in this decomposition (Dashboard is already Konflux-onboarded per architecture context), so the rule is not triggered; a build-pipeline-green AC is included on E001 as good practice.
